accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding minority scholarships:
1. The Pre-matric Scholarship covers Classes IX and X.
2. The income ceiling for the Post-matric Scholarship is parental income below ₹2.5 lakh.
3. The Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is meant for professional and technical undergraduate and postgraduate courses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Pre-matric Scholarship covers Classes IX-X, the Post-matric income ceiling is below ₹2.5 lakh, and Merit-cum-Means covers professional and technical UG-PG courses.
accepted.tq: Test each statement separately, especially the class range, income ceiling and course category.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a provision or associated feature mentioned in relation to the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 and UMEED?

Mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of its income
Uploading property data on the UMEED portal within six months
Audit of waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the Supreme Court’s interim directions of September 2025 concerning waqf provisions?
o: The five-year-practice rule and the Collector’s power were stayed; non-Muslim members were capped at three in State Boards and four in the Central Council.
Only the UMEED portal was stayed, while the five-year-practice rule was upheld without limitation.
All provisions of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 were permanently struck down.
The Collector’s power was transferred to State Boards and non-Muslim membership was capped at four in State Boards and three in the Council.
accepted.x: The interim order stayed the five-year-practice rule and the Collector’s power, and capped non-Muslim members at three in State Boards and four in the Council.
accepted.tq: Separate an interim stay and membership cap from permanent invalidation or transfer of powers.

Consider the following statements regarding the AP State Christian Minorities Finance Corporation:

3. A ₹5,000 honorarium was provided to pastors of 8,427 churches.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the AP State Waqf Board’s 2024-25 assistance and survey?

₹10,000 per month to Imams and ₹5,000 to Mouzzans in 4,984 masjids, costing ₹45 crore; survey completed for 7,005 of 10,522 properties.

accepted.s: Which one of the following accurately describes the status of the Uniform Civil Code in the context stated?
o: Uttarakhand’s UCC has been in force since January 2025; Bills passed by Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh await Presidential assent.
UCC has been in force in all NDA-ruled States since January 2025; no State Bills await assent.
Only Assam’s Bill awaits Presidential assent, while Uttarakhand’s UCC has not yet commenced.
Uttarakhand, Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh all implemented their UCC laws in 2024.
accepted.x: Uttarakhand’s UCC came into force in January 2025, while the Bills of Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh were awaiting Presidential assent.
accepted.tq: Separate an enacted and operative law from Bills that have only been passed and await assent.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Union Home Minister indicated that the Uniform Civil Code could be implemented in all 21 NDA-ruled States by:
accepted.x: The indicated target was implementation of the UCC in all 21 NDA-ruled States by 2029.
accepted.tq: Use exact target-year recall and distinguish an announced timeline from present legal status.

accepted.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised primarily because it:
o: Gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, despite the state-level identification approach associated with T.M.A. Pai.
Transfers all minority identification powers exclusively to State Commissions.
Requires every minority community to be identified only through a census conducted by the Supreme Court.
Prevents the Centre from notifying any minority community.
accepted.x: The criticism is that Section 2(c) gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, whereas T.M.A. Pai is associated with state-level identification.
accepted.tq: Match the legal criticism with the correct authority and constitutional interpretation.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relevant minority institutions and facts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: AP has only a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.28 lakh and Urdu is the third official language.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, but Urdu is not an official language and Christians number 8.62 lakh.
AP has only a Central Minorities Commission and no separate Christian Finance Corporation or Waqf Board.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations, and a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has the stated State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations and a Waqf Board; its Christian population is 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
accepted.tq: Check the complete institutional and numerical combination rather than one isolated fact.

₹2.0 lakh

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding religious enumeration in India is correct?
o: The 2011 Census recorded the Hindu share above 80% and introduced only a ‘No Religion’ category.
The 2011 Census was the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80%, and it also included a ‘No Religion’ option for the first time.
The 2001 Census was the first in which the Hindu share fell below 80%, but it did not include a ‘No Religion’ option.
The 2021 Census was the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80%.
accepted.x: The year 2011 marked both the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80% and the first inclusion of a ‘No Religion’ option.
accepted.tq: Combine two first-occurrence facts tied to the same census year.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Census 2027 enumeration schedule includes which of the following?
o: Only the six notified religions, without any parental information
The six religions plus ‘other religion’, along with the religion and birthplace of both parents
Only ‘No Religion’ and ‘Other Religion’, along with the birthplace of grandparents
The six religions plus caste, but no question on birthplace
accepted.x: The Census 2027 schedule lists the six religions and ‘other religion’, and asks the religion and birthplace of both parents.
accepted.tq: Watch for omissions and substitutions in a list-based enumeration question.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the two debates mentioned in relation to religious minorities?
o: The ‘demography’ narrative versus literacy data; and the over-representation of religious minorities in higher-judiciary appointments.
The ‘demography’ narrative versus fertility data; and the low representation of religious minorities in higher-judiciary appointments.
The ‘migration’ narrative versus rainfall data; and the absence of minorities from all courts.
The ‘demography’ narrative versus urbanisation data; and the representation of minorities exclusively in local courts.
accepted.x: The debates include the demography narrative in relation to fertility data and the fact that religious minorities constitute only about 5% of higher-judiciary appointees.
accepted.tq: Match each debate with its correct comparison and avoid reversing the representation claim.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Religious minorities constitute approximately what share of higher-judiciary appointees?
o: About 15%
About 25%
About 10%
About 5%
accepted.x: Religious minorities account for only about 5% of higher-judiciary appointees.
accepted.tq: Use the approximate percentage as a direct quantitative fact, not as a general representation claim.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

o: Jains
Christians
